feature_sets.name: Platform Core (tenancy, identity, audit, events, jobs, boundaries)
feature_sets.summary: Tenant registry with Postgres RLS, users/roles/scopes, immutable audit trail, number sequences, per-tenant feature flags, transactional outbox + relay, job definitions/runs, idempotency keys, attachments metadata, declarative approvals, document links, custom-field registry, the FinancePort (finance_journal_intent persistence + read API per D2) and the v0 order boundary stub contracts (order.demand@0 / order.supply@0 per D3).
exit_checks: docker compose run --rm api alembic upgrade head
acceptance: Given a request authenticated for tenant A, when it requests a tenant-B resource by id, then the API returns 404 and a raw-SQL read without the tenant GUC returns no row (RLS test matrix on every route).

Given the same Idempotency-Key and request hash submitted twice, when both requests complete, then exactly one resource/outcome exists and the replay returns the stored response; a different hash with the same key returns 409 IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT.

Given a committed domain transaction emitting events, when the outbox relay runs, then events are delivered at-least-once with per-aggregate ordering and consumers deduplicate via event_consumer_checkpoint.

Given NullFinanceAdapter is active, when a value-bearing posting emits a journal intent, then the intent (accounts, debit/credit, currency, dimensions, source document, posting-rule id) is persisted to finance_journal_intent and returned read-only by GET /v1/finance/journal-intents (D2).

Given the order boundary stub contract v0.1.0, when a documented commit/release/fulfill/return command is replayed against the test double, then request/response schemas validate and the inventory-side command shapes are stable (D3).
feature_sets.rollback: Flag off platform.core.enabled blocks every domain write while platform tables stay readable; forward-fix only; migrations are additive and N-1 compatible (no down-migrations in prod); restore from pre-deploy snapshot only if the outbox/audit exit gate fails.

feature_sets.name: Item Master and UoM Engine
feature_sets.summary: Item identity and NetSuite item-type taxonomy with type-specific extensions (inventory/purchasing/sales/accounting), UoM types/units/conversions and per-item UoM sets, item categories, kit/group composition, matrix parent/child items, barcodes/aliases/related items, and per-item/per-location stock and planning attributes (reorder point, preferred stock, safety stock, lead time).
exit_checks: docker compose run --rm api alembic upgrade head
acceptance: Given an item of type INVENTORY, when it is created with a units type and base UoM, then exactly one item_inventory row and one STOCK item_uom row exist and posting eligibility resolves from the type taxonomy.

Given a quantity expressed in a non-base UoM, when the conversion engine normalises it, then it returns a NUMERIC(38,12) base quantity with documented rounding and an unmapped UoM returns 422 UOM_TYPE_MISMATCH.
Given a saved item, when any client or migration attempts to change item_type, costing_method, stock UoM or initial cost, then the database trigger rejects the update (documented immutability D-22).
Given a matrix parent with option values, when a child item is created, then item_matrix_member stores the full option mapping and a second parent for the same child is rejected.
feature_sets.rollback: Flag off inventory.item_master.enabled stops new item writes; existing items remain readable; migrations additive; forward-fix for data issues (no hard delete; inactivate instead).

feature_sets.name: Pricing Engine (item pricing + advanced pricing + effective-date updates)
feature_sets.summary: Price levels, item prices per level/currency with quantity breaks, quantity pricing schedules and calculation modes, pricing groups, customer groups (external refs), price rules with criteria/actions and dynamic item collections, coupons, and effective-date price updates with overlap exclusion (EXT, D4) — resolves immutable price snapshots for documents.
exit_checks: docker compose run --rm api alembic upgrade head
acceptance: Given coupon, price-rule, pricing-group, price-level and base-price data for one item, when a price is resolved, then the documented precedence (coupon -> rule priority with conflict policy -> pricing group -> level -> base) is applied deterministically and the source is recorded.

Given overlapping effective-date price updates for the same target/level/currency, when the second update is saved, then the overlap exclusion constraint rejects it or marks the earlier one SUPERSEDED per documented handling.
Given an applied effective-date update, when its start date arrives, then new item_price rows become effective and previously stored document price snapshots are unchanged.
Given quantity pricing with LINE/OVERALL_ITEM/PARENT/SCHEDULE modes, when a line quantity crosses a break, then the calculation matches the golden dataset for every mode.
feature_sets.rollback: Flag off pricing.engine.enabled; document creation falls back to explicit prices; additive migrations; price updates reversible via REVERTED status, never by deleting rows.

feature_sets.name: Storage and Inventory-Status Registry
feature_sets.summary: Location registry (hierarchy, type, bins/statuses/consignment flags, per-line locations, exactly one UNALLOCATED bootstrap sentinel), zones and bins, and the inventory-status registry whose flags are the single source of availability/commitment/sellability semantics.
exit_checks: docker compose run --rm api alembic upgrade head
acceptance: Given a bootstrap tenant, when the registry migration/seed completes, then exactly one location has is_unallocated=true and it validates location_type=UNALLOCATED.
Given a location with bins disabled, when a bin or bin-scoped posting position is requested, then the API rejects it with 422 BINS_NOT_ENABLED / location rule.
Given an inventory status with is_committable=false, when a commitment is attempted against stock in that status, then the ledger rejects it with 409 STATUS_NOT_COMMITTABLE.
Given a tenant with a default status, when no status is supplied on a posting, then the tenant default status is applied deterministically.
feature_sets.rollback: Flag off inventory.storage_registry.enabled blocks new location/bin/status changes; existing references stay valid; additive migrations; master data is inactivated, never deleted.

feature_sets.name: Inventory Ledger Core (posting, balances, commitments, transfers, adjustments, imports)
feature_sets.summary: Append-only inventory transaction headers/lines/details with the atomic posting engine, synchronously maintained balances and availability, commitments/allocations and the external order boundary commands (commit/release/reallocate/fulfil/return), one-step and transfer-order flows with in-transit, adjustments/absolute worksheets, UNALLOCATED bootstrap distribution, reason codes and the idempotent import contract.
exit_checks: docker compose run --rm api alembic upgrade head
acceptance: Given an approved adjustment/transfer/receipt posting command with an Idempotency-Key, when it posts, then exactly one inventory_transaction plus signed lines/details and balance updates commit atomically and a retry returns the same transaction id.

Given any posting, when the exit-gate invariant query runs, then sum(line.qty_base) equals the balance delta per posting key (INV-01) and no balance references the UNALLOCATED location after bootstrap.

Given available stock and a commit command from the external order boundary, when it is accepted, then qty_committed rises by exactly q and a release/reallocate restores availability without ledger rows.
Given a transfer order, when it is approved/fulfilled/received/closed, then source on-hand, destination in-transit and destination on-hand move per T-10/T-11 and C-04/C-05 with the expected events.
Given an import batch with one invalid row, when it posts, then valid rows are posted idempotently, the invalid row is reported with its error, and the batch ends PARTIAL.
feature_sets.rollback: Flag off inventory.ledger.enabled blocks posting writes; append-only ledger rows are never deleted — corrections are compensating postings; additive migrations stay N-1 compatible.

feature_sets.name: Costing and Valuation Engine
feature_sets.summary: Cost objects and methods (average, FIFO, LIFO, standard, specific, lot, group-average), cost layers and consumption trail, append-only cost ledger, recalculation engine with per-tenant block/provisional policy (D5), standard cost categories/templates/versions/rollup/revaluation, variances, landed/estimated landed cost, COGS adjustments, location costing groups and value reconciliation.
exit_checks: docker compose run --rm api alembic upgrade head
acceptance: Given a posted receipt, when the costing engine runs inside the posting transaction, then each movement's value delta equals qty x the method-deterministic unit cost and the cost ledger entry links to the ledger line.

Given an item with a pending recalculation and costing.block_when_recalc_pending=true, when a posting requires a provisional cost, then the API returns 409 COSTING_RECALC_REQUIRED and nothing is posted (D5).

Given a FIFO/LIFO item, when layers are consumed across receipts, then the append-only consumption trail reconstructs the exact remaining layer state and a nightly reconcile compares cost ledger to item_cost with zero drift.
Given a standard-cost revaluation or landed-cost application, when it posts value-only movements, then layer/avg state updates and the finance intent carries the correct posting-rule dimension.
Given group-average costing, when an inventory worksheet is attempted for a group item, then the documented incompatibility guard rejects it (D6).
feature_sets.rollback: Flag off costing.engine.enabled; postings fall back to a provisional-cost block (default) instead of writing values; additive migrations; recalculations and valuations are rerunnable/idempotent, corrections via compensating value postings only.

feature_sets.name: Numbered Inventory (lots and serials)
feature_sets.summary: Lot and serial identity registries, serial current projection plus append-only serial history, expiry/FEFO attributes, specific-cost identity, and the deferred-FK backfill that closes ledger/costing lot/serial references created nullable in earlier sets.
exit_checks: docker compose run --rm api alembic upgrade head
acceptance: Given a serialized item receipt with N serials, when it posts, then N serial_number rows and N append-only serial_number_history rows exist and the sum of ledger detail for serialized positions equals the serial count (INV-18).
Given a lot-numbered item with expiry, when FEFO allocation runs, then earlier-expiry lots are recommended first and picking an expired lot is rejected with 422 LOT_EXPIRED.

Given deferred lot/serial FK columns created by FS-04/FS-05, when the FS-06 migration runs, then every existing row backfills to NULL-or-valid identity, FK constraints validate, and the orphan check returns zero.
Given a serialized item, when a posting is attempted with a line/serial quantity mismatch, then the posting is rejected with 409 SERIAL_QTY_MISMATCH and nothing is written.
feature_sets.rollback: Flag off inventory.numbered.enabled blocks new numbered-item posting; existing lot/serial rows remain readable and FKs stay additive; forward-fix only (no removal of validated constraints in prod).

feature_sets.name: Inventory Counts and Cycle Counts
feature_sets.summary: Count plans/filters and cycle-count scheduling, physical and cycle count aggregates with immutable on-hand snapshot, line capture/recount, approve/reject/recalculation handling, and variance posting (T-20) with documented numbered/consigned/group-average routing.
exit_checks: docker compose run --rm api alembic upgrade head
acceptance: Given a count plan on a bin/item scope, when a count is generated, then count lines snapshot on-hand at generation time and later postings do not change the snapshot.
Given an approved count with variances, when it posts, then T-20 writes one COUNT_VARIANCE transaction per count whose per-line delta equals counted minus snapshot and costing values it per method.

Given an approved-then-recalculated count (documented rejection path), when the snapshot recalculates, then only unposted counted quantities are considered and the original snapshot is retained for audit.

Given a count line for a serialized/consigned position, when variance posting is requested via the wrong path, then the documented prohibition routes it to adjustment/consigned posting (409 PROHIBITED_COUNT_TYPE).
feature_sets.rollback: Flag off inventory.counts.enabled blocks new counts and variance posting; count snapshots/decisions stay readable for audit; additive migrations; corrections via compensations, never deletes.

feature_sets.name: Procurement (vendor master, P2P documents, receipts, bills, returns)
feature_sets.summary: Vendor master and item-vendor pricing/contracts, requisitions/purchase requests/RFQ with declarative approvals, PO lifecycle (standard/blanket/drop-ship/special-order), receipts with T-01/T-02, vendor bills/variance/3-way match T-04/T-06, credits T-05, vendor returns T-03, drop-ship T-28 and special-order links, all posting through the FS-04 ledger and FS-05 costing contracts.
exit_checks: docker compose run --rm api alembic upgrade head
acceptance: Given an approved PO line for 10 units, when two partial receipts post, then open qty decreases by each receipt, over-receipt beyond tolerance is rejected, and po.receipted events carry cumulative quantities.

Given a receipt-matched vendor bill, when it posts, then it is value-only (no qty change), bill qty <= received qty is enforced, variance rows are created within tolerance, and the finance intent records the accrual reclass.
Given a vendor return authorization, when it ships, then T-03 removes on-hand at the item method cost and the RA line tracks shipped vs authorized quantities.

Given a drop-ship/special-order PO linked to external demand via order.demand external_ref, when it is fulfilled, then T-28 posts value-only with no inventory movement and the special_order_link is unique per external line.
Given a PO whose receipt was fully billed, when the PO is closed, then no line retains open qty or unposted receipt state.
feature_sets.rollback: Flag off procurement.p2p.enabled blocks new document creation/posting; posted documents remain immutable and readable; additive migrations; corrections via reversal/credit documents, no deletes.

feature_sets.name: Manufacturing (assembly/BOM, work orders, WIP, routing, scheduling inputs)
feature_sets.summary: Assembly item extensions, BOM/revisions/component control, phantom explosion, routings/work centres/calendars and cost templates, work-order lifecycle (planned/firm/release/in-process/built/closed/void), WIP issue/completion/close T-17/T-18/T-19, assembly build/unbuild T-15/T-16, outsourced operations, ECOs, scheduling runs/capacity data (computation + API only; Scheduler UI deferred, D4) and available-to-build calculation (EXT, D4).
exit_checks: docker compose run --rm api alembic upgrade head
acceptance: Given a released work order with component requirements, when a WIP issue posts, then component on-hand decreases at the WIP location, WIP value rises, and a work_order_wip_balance read model reconciles to the postings.
Given a build/unbuild command, when it posts, then T-15/T-16 consumes/restores components per the effective BOM revision and any value difference posts to the unbuild variance cost category.
Given a WIP work order on a LIFO/FIFO/specific-cost assembly, when WIP is enabled for that item, then the documented incompatibility guard rejects the configuration (D6).

Given a scheduling run request with finite/infinite and forward/backward parameters, when it executes, then scheduled_operation/capacity_plan/work_center_load rows are written deterministically for the same inputs and no UI is required (D4).

Given an item with a BOM and on-hand components, when GET /v1/available-to-build is called, then the calculation returns buildable quantity from the documented inputs (EXT, D4) and is covered by deterministic fixtures.
feature_sets.rollback: Flag off manufacturing.wip.enabled then manufacturing.enabled; open WOs must be closed/voided before disabling; posted WIP/build documents are immutable; additive migrations; forward-fix only.

feature_sets.name: Replenishment and Planning (AIM, demand, supply/MRP, DRP, allocation, ATP)
feature_sets.summary: Planning rules/scopes and time fences, demand history and statistical demand plans, supply/MRP plans with suggestions and action messages, DRP network/bill-of-distribution on the same engine, supply-allocation strategies/runs with FEFO, versioned AIM reorder-point/preferred-stock formula policy (D7), and ATP projections/query API with versioned method policy (D7); order creation is explicit draft creation through FS-08/FS-09/FS-04 APIs and planning never posts inventory.
exit_checks: docker compose run --rm api alembic upgrade head
acceptance: Given a tenant with an AIM formula policy id+version, when replenishment.aim runs, then every replenishment_calculation_line records formula_version and deterministic fixtures produce the same reorder point/preferred stock as the policy contract (D7).

Given open demands and supplies, when a supply plan runs, then supply_plan_line projected balances and suggestions are produced and POST /v1/supply-plans/{id}/create-orders creates drafts only via FS-08/FS-09/FS-04 APIs (no ledger rows from planning).

Given allocation strategies and FEFO lots, when an allocation run executes, then allocation_result never exceeds supply by item/location or lot, and unsatisfied demand raises allocation_exception records.

Given an ATP method policy, when GET /v1/atp is queried, then earliest availability and per-bucket projections are returned per the versioned method semantics and projected available is clamped at zero.
Given planning runs, when they complete twice from identical inputs, then results are deterministic and a rerun creates a new immutable run (idempotent run_key).
feature_sets.rollback: Flag off replenishment.planning.enabled stops jobs/APIs; plans/results remain readable and immutable; draft documents created from suggestions remain owned by their contexts; additive migrations.

feature_sets.name: Warehouse Management Execution (server-side tasks only)
feature_sets.summary: Warehouse extensions of locations, item process families/groups/stock locations, order types/UCC formats/carrier service levels, pick/putaway strategies and system rules, bin blocking, inbound shipments/receiving orders/putaway tasks, waves/release schedules, pick/pack/ship tasks and ship manifests, WMS replenishment and status-change tasks, and backend cart/device-session records (EXT; no mobile UI/protocol, D8).
exit_checks: docker compose run --rm api alembic upgrade head
acceptance: Given a released order line, when a wave releases it, then pick tasks decompose per strategy/rules and PATCH task completion posts the corresponding ledger movements (bin transfer/status change/fulfillment) through FS-04 contracts only.
Given a blocked bin or an expired lot, when a pick task recommendation is generated, then the bin/lot is excluded and an exception state is recorded instead of a negative or expired pick.

Given an inbound shipment and a receiving order, when receiving completes with deferred posting enabled, then item_receipt moves to PENDING_POSTING and manual post/reversal flows use FS-08 receipt contracts.
Given cart/device_session records exist, when any mobile-specific protocol or offline sync endpoint is requested, then the API has none (D8); only server-side task/queue resources are exposed.
Given WMS replenishment planning/execution, when a replenishment task completes, then it posts a bin transfer (T-29) and updates the primary bin quantity read model.
feature_sets.rollback: Flag off wms.execution.enabled blocks task creation/completion; tasks remain as records for audit; posted movements are immutable (corrective postings only); additive migrations.

feature_sets.name: Quality Management (specs, inspections, COA) — SuiteApp semantics backend
feature_sets.summary: Quality specs/lines, inspection plans/lines, event triggers and on-demand inspection queues, inspection instances/results with disposition and waiver, COA headers/lines, quality images via attachment metadata, and preference/derived-field configuration — backend data/logic only per D4 (quality REST API, mobile collection and reports deferred).
exit_checks: docker compose run --rm api alembic upgrade head
acceptance: Given an inspection trigger configured on receipts and a posted receipt, when the trigger evaluates, then exactly one inspection is created for the source document and its queue entry is idempotent per event.

Given an inspection with required spec lines, when all results are recorded, then PASS/FAIL disposition derives from results and a FAIL can only be closed by approved WAIVE or an inventory hold posting via FS-04.
Given a quality hold, when it is applied, then the affected stock is moved to a non-committable status through the ledger status-change contract (T-30) and availability changes accordingly.
Given a passed inspection/COA, when a COA is generated, then it references the inspection and its result lines and is immutable after issue.
feature_sets.rollback: Flag off quality.management.enabled blocks new inspections/triggers/COA writes; holds already applied remain as status postings and are not auto-released by the flag; additive migrations.

feature_sets.name: Consigned Inventory Management
feature_sets.summary: Vendor consignment agreements and covered items/locations, consigned ownership receipts T-21 and ownership-transfer-on-consumption T-22, consigned adjustments/counts T-23, consumption audit trail feeding reporting, finance intents for consigned accounts, and the documented consigned-vs-assembly incompatibility guard (D6).
exit_checks: docker compose run --rm api alembic upgrade head
acceptance: Given an ACTIVE consignment agreement and an allowed item, when a consigned receipt posts (T-21), then qty rises under ownership=CONSIGNED with no AP liability and a consigned valuation entry.

Given consigned on-hand, when consumption/ownership transfer posts (T-22), then the same qty moves CONSIGNED->OWNED, a vendor bill is created through the FS-08 contract, and consignment_consumption records the audit row.

Given a tenant that enables consigned inventory, when an assembly item is configured for consignment or manufacturing is enabled, then the documented incompatibility guard rejects the configuration (D6).

Given consigned stock, when an inventory worksheet or ordinary adjustment path is attempted, then the consigned routing (T-23) is enforced and the ordinary path returns 409 PROHIBITED_CONSIGNED_OPERATION.
feature_sets.rollback: Flag off consigned.inventory.enabled blocks new consigned postings; existing consigned positions remain valued/readable; use T-22/T-23 for disposition before disabling; additive migrations.

feature_sets.name: Extensions (warranty, customer part numbers, UPC registry)
feature_sets.summary: Backend-only SuiteApp semantics included by D4: item warranty terms and warranty registration/claims/actions/repair-order data, customer part number mappings to items, and the Auto Assign UPC registry (assignment/retirement/monitoring) — no UI/workbook, no external integrations.
exit_checks: docker compose run --restart=no api alembic upgrade head
acceptance: Given an item with default warranty terms, when a warranty registration is created for a serialized unit, then the registration validates the serial identity (FS-06) and the coverage window/terms derive from the item terms.

Given a registration and claim, when a claim is validated, then it is rejected outside coverage unless approved as an override, and repair/refund/replacement actions are recorded append-only on the claim.

Given Auto Assign UPC enabled for a tenant, when two items are assigned UPCs, then the registry enforces uniqueness and retirement frees a UPC for assignment tracking but never reuses the item/UPC history row.
Given a customer part number mapping, when a duplicate mapping is inserted, then the (tenant, customer_ref, part_number) uniqueness rule rejects it.
feature_sets.rollback: Flag off extensions.registry.enabled blocks new registrations/claims/UPC assignments; existing records readable; additive migrations; corrections via new claim actions/registrations, never deletes.

feature_sets.name: Reporting Read Models and Reporting API
feature_sets.summary: Read-only reporting schemas/views and query APIs over the read models of all prior sets: stock ledger, valuation summary/detail, current snapshot, back-order, activity detail, pending fulfillment, turnover and profitability inputs, balance/detail search, ATP/workbench views — no writes and no analytics UI (D1, framework §1).
exit_checks: docker compose run --rm api alembic upgrade head
acceptance: Given a posted ledger/cost history, when reporting views/materialised views refresh, then valuation summary/detail, stock ledger, snapshot, back-order and pending-fulfillment results reconcile exactly to the underlying read models (zero drift).
Given any reporting endpoint, when a write verb is attempted, then the API returns 405/403 and the reporting schema grants reject writes (read-only contract).
Given balance/detail search endpoints, when queried with tenant+dimension+date filters, then results respect RLS, cursor pagination and the p95 read budget.
Given a read-model refresh failure, when the job retries, then the previous snapshot remains served and an alert/reporting.view.refreshed failure metric is raised.
feature_sets.rollback: Flag off reporting.readmodels.enabled leaves views in place but stops refreshes/APIs; views are droppable/recreatable without touching base tables; no data migrations in this set.
